outcomes: Apply course concepts in the analysis of case studies.
Explain how ethnicity, gender, and age influence the etiology and diagnosis of psychological disorders and access to treatment.
Explain how changes in individual thoughts and behaviors and family systems may reduce the risk of mental disorders.

rows.title: Introduction to Psychology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: PART 2:
Compare and contrast major theoretical perspectives of psychology and explain how to apply these perspectives to personal and professional life.
Describe the scientific process within psychological research, the APA standards for writing, the major ethical guidelines, and the impact of diversity on psychological research.
Explain human behavior as a function of biological, cognitive, and socio-cultural factors.

rows.title: Introduction to Sociology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will identify and apply the main sociological theoretical frameworks to analyze social stratification based on race, ethnicity, gender, social class, sexuality or other social groups.
Students will apply sociological research to distinguish the interrelatedness of various social intuitions.
Students will identify the role of culture and socialization in the development of one’s beliefs, opinions, and values.

rows.title: Honors Social Problems
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Students will be able to identify and analyze how sociological principles, concepts, and categories (e.g. age, gender, class, race, ethnicity, sexual orientation, etc.) are applied in the understanding of social problems.
Students will determine the causes and the extent of social trends and problems such as racial discrimination, poverty, social violence, immigration, gender inequality, and crime.

Students will identify and explain the extent and consequences of current social issues and problems in the US and globally through the interpretation of data describing social changes in the areas of family, work, school, religion, and/or the economy.

rows.title: The Sociology of Health, Illness, and Healing
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Systematically apply sociological methods and theories to the study of health, illness, and healthcare delivery within specific and diverse communities.

Access and analyze a range of primary (gathered via interviews, surveys, site visits, participant observation, etc.) and secondary (e.g., relevant historical and contemporary research, government data sets, public policy documents, web-based resources, etc.) data sources available to sociologists, public-health professionals, and consumers.
Apply different sociological methods/theories to examine and interpret class materials in the context of a community-based research experience.
Assess/Evaluate the strengths and weakness of a particular research topic or healthcare program/intervention.
Summarize and communicate research results for diverse audiences.

rows.title: Honors Elementary Spanish II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use appropriate grammatical structures that include advanced vocabulary, verb conjugations, and regional usage of common lexicon.
Write more complex paragraphs, dialogues, and compositions with an enhanced level of appropriate syntax and grammar.
Read, analyze, and express personal opinions in Spanish on a set number of cultural topics.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on a variety of topics related to the Spanish-speaking world.
Demonstrate a higher level of critical thinking and professionalism in presentations.  (*Honors)

rows.title: Honors Intermediate Spanish I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write multiple compositions in Spanish at the intermediate level using description, summary, comparisons, and other modes.
Demonstrate understanding of critical analysis of literary material.
Express personal opinions and perspectives in Spanish on specific readings.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on topics related to cultural aspects of the Spanish-speaking world.
Demonstrate a higher level of critical thinking and professionalism in presentations. (*Honors)
Produce advanced-level analytical essays demonstrating academic fluency in various literary topics. (*Honors)

rows.title: College Spanish Composition
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate understanding of critical analysis of literary material.
Incorporate idiomatic expressions and literary concepts.
Produce college-level academic writing in Spanish demonstrating academic fluency in various literary topics with correct MLA format and documentation.

rows.title: Introduction to Theatre
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Assess components of plays.
Identify the roles and responsibilities for each artistic team member in a theatre production.
Develop dialogue with a beginning, middle and end, to support the role of the playwright.

rows.title: Intermediate Acting
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Measure personal acting process and the use of various acting techniques.
Utilize range and flexibility in voice performance, improvisation, auditioning, and scene work.
Collaborate in seeking common solutions to acting tasks.

rows.title: Fundamentals of Scene Study
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Define, recall and select the characteristics of style as it applies to period and contemporary stage plays.
Utilize interactive listening strategies as it pertains to the use of stylized theatrical language and comedic timing.
Identify, develop, and utilize character objectives, obstacles, and tactics when developing character choices for varying styles and periods.

rows.title: Introduction to Lighting Design
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Critique personal and peer installation techniques.
Apply design concepts in the creation of a lighting design.
Use safety procedures to ensure a safe working environment for all actors, stage crew, and audience members.

rows.title: Technical Production
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Execute command calls from the stage manager with accuracy.
Utilize concepts learned in rehearsals to execute assigned technical responsibilities during performance.
Perform assigned tasks at all technical rehearsals and performances.

rows.title: Theatre Performance
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate skills working within a professional framework of collaboration.
Support the behavioral life of a character in performance.
Evaluate a script for performance.

rows.title: Tour Ensemble
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Develop character analyses and biographies.
Score dialogue and character arc in a script.
Use clear pronunciation, articulation, and appropriate vocal techniques in performance.

rows.title: Intermediate Stage Lighting
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Interpret multiple control console manuals for information as it applies to the automation of stage lighting.
Complete control and programming tasks.
Evaluate a conventional and automated light plot to determine the location and fixture type.

rows.title: Musical Theatre Techniques
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Appraise a resume, portfolio, and headshot.
Demonstrate vocal clarity.
Justify character motivation.

rows.title: Voice for the Actor
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Rate physical and vocal skills.
Utilize optimal conditioning of the voice as it relates to a theatrical presentation.
Interpret vocal coloring, projection, diction, rhythm, and phrasing.

rows.title: Introduction to Diesel-Electric Technology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Recognize and identify the primary parts and operation of diesel engines, electrical drivetrains, and hybrid systems found in heavy-duty transportation.
Interpret labor market information to understand current employment conditions, wages, and workforce opportunities in the diesel-electric transportation field.

Identify safety practices and regulations (CARB, EPA, DOT, OSHA) regarding diesel, electric, and hybrid transportation systems and how it relates to future technical training and career investigation.

rows.title: Electrical Fundamentals
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use Ohm's law to determine voltage, amperage, and resistance in a series, parallel, and/or series-parallel circuit.
Inspect a relay circuit to determine proper operation and diagnose a faulty relay.
Test a battery, starter, and alternator using diagnostic tools and equipment.

rows.title: Introduction to Computer Software & Online Applications
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Launch a software or online application from the start menu or desktop shortcuts.
Create or edit files in a software or online application.
Save and print documents in a software or online application.

rows.title: Introduction to Customer Service Skills
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Analyze customer service needs and select responses that demonstrate high quality customer service.
Convey information in a meaningful and respectful way, such as avoiding certain phrases and speak in a straightforward manner using everyday language that customers can understand.
Exhibit various strategies to handle challenging customers with professionalism and empathy.
Incorporate activities in their daily life to relieve stress caused by performing customer service duties.

rows.title: Orientation to Computers
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create, save, rename, delete, and restore a file and folder.
Recognize that mice can be customized for left-handed people and that speed of clicking can also be customized.
Locate files and folders in Windows File Explorer.
Demonstrate appropriate use and ability to right-click, left-click, and double click.

rows.title: Accounting Terminology
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Research current online job listings in both the private and public sector and discuss qualifications required for each job.
Define and explain debits and credits, double entry bookkeeping, chart of accounts, and financial statements.

rows.title: Adobe Photoshop
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Implement the basic image editing workflow from image acquisition to output.
Properly prepare any source image file for different output media (e.g., print, web, email, etc.).
Produce images for their unique business application by using the tools and creative techniques available through Photoshop's toolbar and menu options.

rows.title: Human Resources Operations
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Create and deploy HR Policies and Procedures for effective HR management.
Navigate and utilize Human Resources Information Systems (HRIS) for managing employee data and HR processes.
Explain payroll practices and compliance requirements.
Administer benefits and compensation programs.

rows.title: Workforce Power Skills
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Engage with others to enhance team effectiveness.
Speak in a professional manner, use appropriate content, and say things in a way that others will understand.

rows.title: Digital Literacy for Academic and Professional Success - Tier 3
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Communicate on social media to understand the impact of one's digital footprint.
Use social media for career development.
Use wiki or blogging technology to organize artifacts or information

rows.title: Systems and Networking Essentials
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Plan and install a home or small business network using wireless technology, then connect it to the Internet.
Develop critical thinking and problem-solving skills using Cisco Packet Tracer.
Practice verifying and troubleshooting network and Internet connectivity.
Recognize and mitigate security threats to a home network.

rows.title: Vocational Construction Technology Module II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Read, comprehend, and explain blueprints, safety charts, and diagrams.
Use quantitative and qualitative data to estimate materials and resources needed in construction.
Plan and complete a project by using tools and materials to build it.

rows.title: Introduction to the Fashion Industry
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Write a critique of a fashion career.

rows.title: ServSafe® Food Protection Manager Certification Exam Preparation, Review, & Practice
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Complete the ServSafe Food Protection Manager Certification Exam.
Identify principles of food sanitation and safety.
Explain the causes and controls of food borne illnesses.
Identify principles of food sanitation and safety.

rows.title: Dance Laboratory I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Apply critical analysis of performance skills.
Memorize and demonstrate technical and performance dance skills necessary for beginning level dance projects.

rows.title: Musical Theatre Dance Techniques I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate various beginner level technical and performance dance skills in a musical theatre rehearsal and performance setting.
Demonstrate basic skillset in acting choices through dance using script analysis, character research, reflection, and revision through the rehearsal process.
Identify the historical context, roles, work, and values of various influential theatrical dance genres, dancers, and choreographers.
Demonstrate the appropriate preparation needed for an ensemble dancing role specified in a musical theatre audition setting.

rows.title: Showcase I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Gain practical experience in using their imaginations to develop character interpretations.
Evaluate their own acting skills based on the critique and support that they have received during class.
Participate in ensemble acting assignments to recognize the importance of both collaboration and diversity in seeking common solutions to acting tasks.

rows.title: Dance Production I
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate soft skills appropriate in the production of a dance concert.
Memorize and identify dance production terminology and theater etiquette rules.
Execute technical skills and expressive performance skills of a full length dance choreographed by faculty and/or student.
Use critical writing skills to analyze one’s own technical and performance skills to improve different performance roles.

rows.title: Jazz Dance II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify ballet and jazz dance vocabulary appropriate to level II to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to analyze and criticize one’s own technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to jazz dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a jazz dance concert performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to jazz dance level II.

rows.title: Hip-Hop Dance II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Memorize and identify hip-hop dance vocabulary appropriate to level II to recognize and interpret verbal and written instruction.
Demonstrate technical skills and expressive performance skills appropriate to hip-hop dance level II.
Use critical writing skills to complete personal critique and reflection of a hip-hop dance performance.
Discuss and interpret elements of dance composition appropriate to hip-hop dance level II.

rows.title: Certified Nursing Assistant (CNA) Training- Skills Lab
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Identify the roles and responsibilities of a CNA.
Apply effective interpersonal communication skills.
Identify the basic rules of body mechanics and patient positioning.
Identify standard precautions and basic principles related to infection prevention.
Identify metric system, weights, and military time.
Demonstrate ability to care for patients, including bathing, dressing, overall hygiene, feeding, ambulating, and toileting.
Accurately measure and record vital signs, height, weight and state normal parameters of each.

rows.title: Acute Care Nursing Assistant Skills Lab
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Describe and implement proper care for patients in an acute care setting.
Exhibit proficient communication, interpersonal, and documentation abilities to enhance patient care.
Collaborate with licensed nursing staff to assess and monitor patients in an acute care setting, providing valuable support in the healthcare team.

rows.title: BLS for Healthcare Providers & Heartsaver CPR/ First Aid
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Perform CPR.
For BSL, perform multiresucer resuscitation.
Safely use an automated external defibrillator.
Relieve foreign body airway obstruction.

rows.title: Introductory Biotech Lab
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Have a fundamental overview of the lab skills and principles of biotechnology.

rows.title: Elementary Vietnamese II
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Use appropriate grammatical structures that include advanced vocabulary, verb markers, and regional usage of common lexicon.
Write more complex paragraphs, dialogues, and compositions with an enhanced level of appropriate syntax and grammar.
Read, analyze, and express personal opinions on a diverse set of cultural topics.
Engage in oral discussions by actively listening and speaking on a variety of topics related to the Vietnamese-speaking world.

rows.title: Introduction to Gas Tungsten Arc Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and the industrial environment.
Recognize Gas Tungsten Arc Welding equipment and set up.
Perform Gas Tungsten Arc Welding techniques in the 1G, 1F, and 2F positions on carbon steel and alloys.

rows.title: Intermediate Pipe Welding
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Identify different size tube and piping.
Perform pipe welding techniques in the 5G and 6G positions.

rows.title: Structural Welding FCAW
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Demonstrate safety standards and rules given in this course that apply to welding equipment, work habits, and industrial environment.
Create welds in the vertical (3G) and overhead (4G) positions using the flux cored arc welding process.
Reconstruct an AWS D1.1 unlimited thickness test plate.

rows.title: Introduction to Women's Studies
rows.heading: Student Learning Outcomes
rows.lead: At the conclusion of this course, the student should be able to:
outcomes: Distinguish, explain and evaluate the differences between sex and gender.
Describe and analyze the various issues, stages and impacts of the women’s movements in the United States.

Critically analyze and explain how the social construction of gender affects and is affected by the following: language, the family, academic education, the media, employment, politics, law, history, religion and health.
